proposed_sfd_edits.args: 1024  -- implemented by investigations/puritan/tools/ff_scale_em.py <in.sfd> <out.sfd> --int-underline. It ports FontForge 20100501 PyFF_Font_set_em (python.c:11508): ds = newem*Descent/(Ascent+Descent) in INTEGER division, as = newem-ds. Then SFScaleToEm (splinefont.c:506): every OS2*/Hhead*/LineGap field becomes rint(v*scale), offset-mode deltas included; UnderlinePosition and UnderlineWidth are multiplied by scale and written rounded to integers. Then FVTrans (fontviewbase.c:649): every Width and VWidth is truncated (int16 = float); references to selected glyphs have only their offsets scaled; the Back layer is scaled but not rounded. Points go through TransformPoint (single precision, snapped to 1/1024; splineutil.c:1760) and then SCRound2Int/SplinePointRound on Fore (splinechar.c:834/696). An implied point (flag 128, ttfindex -1) becomes the midpoint of its rounded controls. Any other point rounds me and each control's OFFSET from me; order2 controls propagate to the neighbour, and the first-processed point wins. A control rounded onto its point makes the spline a line (SplineRefigure2, splineorder2.c:1229). Fore reference offsets are rint'd. Line count and point flags are preserved.

proposed_converter_changes.description: babelfont convertors/fontforge.rs parse_metric! parses UnderlinePosition/UnderlineWidth (and every metric it handles) as i32 and silently drops a real. FontForge stores sf->upos/uwidth as real and writes them with %g (sfd.c:1838). It exports post.underlinePosition = putshort(upos - uwidth/2) and underlineThickness = putshort(uwidth), both C float-to-int truncation (tottf.c:4116). The proposal: parse these two as f64 and apply that rule in --fontforge-underline-position. Needed only if the scaleem edit keeps FontForge's exact reals (-136.192/20.48); the proposed integer form (-136/20) does not need it. None of the 42 families.tsv sources states a real underline value today, so priority is low.

verification.summary: FINDINGS (FINDINGS.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused report .md files for this subagent, so the full content is here). **Model**: Claude Opus 5.5. CONCLUSION: The Puritan release is not provenance and not a different revision. It is exactly the four .sfd files at googlefontdirectory-hg 52f780bc, run through that tree's own ofl/puritan/src/generate.py under FontForge 20100501. The script exports the .otf at em 1000, then runs f.em = 1024 and f.is_quadratic = True (a no-op, since the Fore layers are already order2). It runs f.round() (a no-op, because it acts on the selection, which is empty at that point), then autoHint and autoInstr, and exports the .ttf. The prior notes (B6-RESIDUALS 'source generation this repo no longer holds', WHATS_NEEDED, PROVENANCE-NOT-CONVERSION) are wrong on this point. EVIDENCE: (1) Release Puritan-Regular.ttf (google/fonts b5efa9c) is byte-identical to monorepo ofl/puritan/Puritan-Regular.ttf. Italic, Bold and BoldItalic differ only in OS/2 fsType 1->0 (google/fonts 8ccda7bf7 'Fix fsType for 40 font files') and head.checkSumAdjustment. (2) The FFTM FFTimeStamp of every release .ttf is 2010-04-29 03:43:27, which equals LibFF_ModTime 1272512607 in fontforge_full-20100501.tar.bz2 (downloads.sourceforge.net/project/fontforge/fontforge-source/, sha256 ee4928b0df7480c31a422645854d9f3f4f6718dd423b6885bd33e87a8a6edd79). The src/*.otf FFTM sourceModified equals the .sfd ModificationTime (2010-11-26 14:05:32), and the .ttf are stamped 14:09:49-52 in generate.py list order. (3) src/*.otf is FontForge's own export before the em change: UPM 1000, sx/cap 495/640, which equals ff_heights_oracle on the unmodified source. (4) tools/ff_scale_em.py ports what f.em=1024 executes in FontForge 20100501, in single precision. The resulting .sfd reproduces the release glyf point-for-point in order: 234/234/229/229 simple glyphs plus every composite's components and offsets, 237/237 glyphs in each of the 4 styles. Advance widths are 237/237 in all 4 (tools/verify_scaled_points.py, which emulates SSTtfNumberPoints+SSAddPoints). (5) The rounding rules are load-bearing. Widths are truncated (int16 = float, splinechar.c:121): truncation matches 237/237, rint only 107/97/113/113. SplinePointRound (splinechar.c:696) rounds each control's offset from its rounded point: plain per-point rounding, even with implied midpoints kept, matches only 95/90/105/97 of 230/230/225/225 simple glyphs (tools/naive_rounding_check.py). The Python em setter splits the em by integer division (python.c:11527): ds = 1024*200/1000 = 204, as = 820. The typo metrics are then 881/-255, which equal the release. The Font Info dialog (fontinfo.c:2019, rint) gives 819/205, which leaves s_typo_ascender [881,880] and s_typo_descender [-255,-256] (runs/gui-rint). PROPOSED EDIT: one commit on all four .sfd, 'Scale the em to 1024 as src/generate.py did', using a new op scaleem 1024 (tools/ff_scale_em.py --int-underline). It writes the underline as -136/20 rather than FontForge's reals -136.192/20.48, because babelfont f725e6a's parse_metric parses i32 and silently drops reals (runs/exact). FontForge exports (short)(upos-uwidth/2) = -146 and (short)uwidth = 20 either way, so the integer form is lossless. Verified: 19/19/20/20 -> 2/4/3/3 blocking rows, none opened. ITALIC RESIDUAL: us_win_ascent and hhea.ascender are [880,881]. FontForge's in-memory em change scaled Scaron (iso8859-15 slot 0xA6) before caron (slot >255), and only reference offsets are scaled. Scaron's cached reference box therefore stayed as the unscaled caron plus the scaled offset. tools/stale_composite_bbox.py predicts the release glyf header of all 3 composites (Scaron, scaron, yacute) in Regular and Italic exactly; Italic Scaron has header yMax 864 while its outline reaches 881. Italic's tallest glyph is Scaron, so the release's font bbox, and the offset-mode Win/Hhead ascent (delta 0), is Aring's 880. That clips Scaron by 1 unit. A fresh FontForge load of the scaled .sfd would give 881; the converter is not at fault.
